remote.tutorialPre: Prerequisite: a domain hosted on Cloudflare (the free plan is enough)
remote.tutorialStep1: Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com, open Zero Trust in the left menu (first use asks for a team name — pick the Free plan);
remote.tutorialStep2: Left menu Networks → Tunnels, click Create a tunnel, connection type Cloudflared;
remote.tutorialStep3: Name the tunnel (e.g. mam-jarvis) → Save tunnel;
remote.tutorialStep4: On the install page install nothing — copy the token starting with eyJh... shown there;
remote.tutorialStep5: Switch to the Public Hostname tab: subdomain mam, pick your domain, Service HTTP://localhost:9420 → Save (required — skipping it leaves the tunnel Healthy but the hostname unresolved and the address unreachable);
remote.tutorialStep6: Back on this Tuvis page, paste the token into the input and click Save; it is done once the status turns Running.
remote.tutorialPost: The address never changes afterwards; Tuvis downloads cloudflared automatically and keeps it running — no manual install needed.
remote.tutorialDocs: Official step-by-step (Cloudflare docs): Create a tunnel (dashboard)
remote.pinHint: Applies to all external channels: LAN / Quick tunnel / Own domain / External domain; local access on this computer also enters it once (via the LAN address). Click Save to apply; a new device enters it once and stays trusted for 180 days; changing it signs out every device
remote.pinSaved: Saved: all devices must re-enter the access PIN
remote.resetDesc: All connected devices will be disconnected and must re-enter the access PIN; the PIN itself stays unchanged.
remote.devicesHint: Re-binding from the same browser on the same network counts as one device; names default to what the device reports and can be renamed
remote.notice: ⚠ The remote page is equivalent to viewing all session content; the address + access PIN are the key — do not share them. 5 consecutive wrong entries lock PIN input for 10 minutes.
remote.tlsDialogDesc: This will expose all session content to the LAN over plain HTTP. The address is the key — only proceed on a network you trust. The confirmation is long-lived; to revoke it, switch binding back to localhost.
remote.tsWizardPath: Opens the first-time setup wizard: detect → download (official source check) → install → sign in → enable → reachability check
remote.tsPitch: A permanent public address with no domain of your own — Tuvis guides you through Tailscale setup. Follow the system installer and authorization prompts, and click Allow when asked (first-time setup may also need one browser approval, or none). No command line involved.
remote.tsProgressHint: Every step shows its progress and where it is stuck
remote.tsRunningHint: Auto-restores on launch; the address never changes
remote.tsOffHint: This channel is off — Funnel is not enabled, so the fixed address is unreachable; turn it on to enable it again (the address never changes).
remote.tsAddrPermanentHint: The address is fixed and never changes — it comes back automatically once this channel is running again.
remote.tsRecoveringHint: The Tailscale backend is reconnecting (usually 1–2 minutes after a reboot) — your configuration and address stay the same; nothing to do.

tsWizard.title: Tailscale Fixed-URL Setup Wizard
tsWizard.windowsUnverified: ⚠ Windows has been machine-verified from “{{from}}” onward: {{steps}} have not been run end-to-end on a real machine (prefilled from official docs; actual behavior may differ). The start step and everything after it are machine-verified.
tsWizard.downloading: Downloading the installer… (total size unknown, so this shows activity instead of a percentage)
tsWizard.fetchingLoginLink: Getting the login link… (Tuvis only asks Tailscale for a link; it never signs in for you or touches your account)
tsWizard.installing: Installing Tailscale… (installer verified; confirm the system prompt and wait)
tsWizard.aboutTailscale: What is this? Tailscale is a free personal mesh-networking tool: it gives every device a fixed private address, which is why we can hand you a permanent link without you owning a domain. Official site:
tsWizard.repairDescription: Tuvis will ask Tailscale to reopen its connection. This does not change any other serve or Funnel entries. If existing configuration is detected, Tuvis will show a separate preview before changing it.
tsWizard.waitingDnsHint: Public DNS is propagating. This may take a few minutes, up to about {{expected}} minutes; waited: {{elapsed}} minutes.
tsWizard.waitingLocalReady: The local board and Funnel are working. No repeated action is needed.
tsWizard.waitingOverdue: This is taking longer than expected. View the troubleshooting steps; Tuvis will keep checking in the background.
tsWizard.troubleshootingKeepOn: Keep the Tailscale client signed in and this channel switched on.
tsWizard.troubleshootingNetwork: Check your computer’s internet connection, then check that Tailscale and Funnel are available for your account.
tsWizard.troubleshootingChecksContinue: Tuvis will continue checking public DNS automatically. You do not need to click repeatedly or switch the channel off.
tsWizard.troubleshootingRepairOptional: After these checks, you can choose Re-enable connection if you still want to reopen it. Nothing runs until you confirm.
tsWizard.tsPendingChecking: The address is not verified yet. Tuvis will check again automatically.
tsWizard.addressWillAppear: After verification, find the address in Settings → Remote Access → the corresponding channel card.
tsWizard.openingInstaller: The installer is open. Finish it, then return here.
tsWizard.tsTransientHint: A connection failure is usually transient public-network jitter. Tuvis checks again every minute; if it remains broken after 10 minutes, inspect the Tailscale account and Funnel settings before choosing Repair.
tsWizard.actAdmin: Click “Install Tailscale” to open the system installer automatically. Follow its instructions; if authorization is required, enter your administrator password in the system window. After installation, return to Tuvis and click “Refresh status”.
tsWizard.actAdminWinMsi: Your action: the installer lets you choose the install path, then the system prompts for the admin password — the default path is the easiest; installing elsewhere is fine, just remember where
tsWizard.installPathHint: Tuvis looks for Tailscale in two places: the default install directory and the executable registered by the "Tailscale" service — a custom install path works too. If it still shows as not installed afterwards, click Refresh.
tsWizard.actSysExt: Your action: approve the Tailscale system extension in System Settings → Privacy & Security
tsWizard.actLogin: Your action: click "Sign in" and complete Tailscale login in your browser
tsWizard.actLoginNoLink: Your action: click “Get login link” and Tuvis will ask Tailscale for an authorization link (it only hands over the link — never signs in for you, never touches your account) — you complete the login in your browser
tsWizard.actFunnel: Your action: if an approval link appears, approve it once in your browser (your tailnet may not require it)
tsWizard.approvalHint: If an approval link appears, approve it once in your browser (it may not be required):
tsWizard.loginLinkHint: No login link yet — click “Get login link” and Tuvis will have Tailscale generate one (Tuvis never signs in for you and never touches your account; you always complete the login in your browser). If it still does not appear, open the Tailscale app on this machine and click “Log in”, or use “Refresh” above to retry.
tsWizard.maybeNeeded: This step may not be needed: whether a browser approval is required depends on your tailnet policy — no action may be needed at all
tsWizard.tsPendingHint: The public DNS record is not published yet — on first setup this takes about 5–6 minutes (if the address was published before, it usually comes back within a minute); the address is only reachable from outside once the record is live.
tsWizard.tsRepublishHint: Funnel was just re-enabled — the public DNS record is being republished (usually 30 seconds – 1 minute); the address never changes.
tsWizard.tsRecoveringHint: The Tailscale backend is reconnecting (usually 1–2 minutes after a reboot) — your configuration and address stay the same; nothing to do.
tsWizard.writePathUnverifiedMac: ⚠ The write path (enable / revoke / self-heal) is not machine-verified on this platform yet — actual behavior may differ; the read-only probes are verified on macOS 1.102.4 (status / funnel status / get), but the write path has never been run.
tsWizard.writePathUnverifiedOther: ⚠ No probing on this platform: install detection, read-only fields and the write path (enable / revoke / self-heal) have not been machine-verified on Linux and similar platforms — behavior may differ.
tsWizard.completeInInstaller: Complete the installation in the system installer, then return here and refresh the status.
tsWizard.manualInstallHint: Automatic download did not finish. Retry it, or use “Download manually” to get the official package and double-click it in your system downloads folder. After installation, return to Tuvis and click “Refresh status”.
tsWizard.actionFailedUnknown: The action failed without error details. Retry or install manually from your downloads folder.
tsWizard.manualOpenHint: The installer is downloaded and verified. Click “Open downloads folder” in this step, double-click the package to install, then return here and refresh the status.

remote.tsDisableTitle: Revoking also clears other serve entries
remote.tsDisableDescMixed: Revoking clears the Tuvis Funnel config together with {{count}} non-Tuvis serve entr(y/ies) — `tailscale funnel reset` wipes the whole config. Nothing happens until you confirm.
remote.tsDisableDescForeign: The current Funnel config contains no Tuvis entry (the port changed, or the config was taken over externally) — a forced revoke clears every entry listed below. Nothing happens until you confirm.
remote.tsDisableDescUnreadable: The Tailscale backend is reconnecting, so the existing serve config cannot be read right now — the entries that will be cleared cannot be listed. Confirming still wipes the whole serve config (which may include non-Tuvis entries); try again in a moment to see the list first.
